newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First caucus yet to consider final agreements.
newsitem.headline: NZ First caucus yet to consider final agreements.

text.p: New Zealand First MPs held a caucus meeting on Tuesday but did not consider a final coalition agreement with either the conservative National Party or the centre-left Labour Party, leader Winston Peters' spokesman Mike Booker said.
"They have been getting regular updates of progress. There's quite a bit of work still to be done," Booker told Reuters.
He said talks were on track for a deal to be announced next week, in time for Parliament's scheduled resumption on December 10.
Nationalist NZ First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election and is negotiating separately with both National and Labour over the shape of the next government.
Informal coalition negotiations were set to continue on Tuesday afternoon, although a spokesman for Labour leader Helen Clark said a session of formal talks was still pencilled in for 5 p.m.
Labour MPs also held a caucus meeting on Tuesday to be briefed on the progress of the talks and on the outstanding Taranaki Maori land claim which an incoming government will negotiate.

The last round of formal talks was held two weeks ago. Since then informal talks between small groups of MPs have been held to negotiate specific policy areas. These will report back to the formal sessions before being referred to the various caucuses.
"The plan is to get everything wrapped up so that a decision can be announced before the House starts sitting...A certain timetable flows from that," Booker told NZPA earlier.

National Prime Minister Jim Bolger, who returned on Tuesday morning from the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum conference in the Philippines, refused to speculate on how the talks would progress.
National's regular Tuesday caucus was cancelled but is likely to be held later in the week.
